summary: Re-cut the Head Swap and Draw It In 4/5 tiles so the seam bisects the subject's face. Plates recovered from Fabio's own runs via the sidecars (mpi-546-smoke t2i_008 + flowHeadSwap_002; Untitled run 015 + its two inputs). Stills only - no hero rebuild, no registry change.

SHIPPED. flow-head-swap.webp 47,706 B and flow-draw-it-in.webp 94,918 B, both 896x1120 webp q90, both well under the 250 KB ceiling. Head Swap seam measured at 50.0% of tile width, on the nose bridge, with the before/after plates proved registered first (mean abs diff 0.49/255, changed bbox x 771-943 y 122-267 = the head alone). Draw It In seam at 25.7%, through the drawn woman's face, on a 1.28x punch that keeps the full figure, its contact shadow, the second woman and the tiger. Both judged at 220 px under the grid's own saturate(.92) brightness(.92). Colours were SAMPLED off the shipped pair rather than picked: bar #FF5FA2, blob flat #E0436B. Heroes and flowsRegistry.js untouched - same filenames, so the descriptors already point at the new bytes.

Closed on Fabio's own confirmation - a card whose whole question is whether two pictures read correctly. Both tiles re-cut so the before/after seam bisects the subject's face: Head Swap on the nose bridge (50.0% of tile), Draw It In through the drawn woman's face (25.7%). Evidence in validation.md.
